URGENT investigation + fix for Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting platform, staging tree /opt/nxeon-staging — work ONLY in staging, never /opt/nxeon prod. Never run `npm run build`; verify only with `npx tsc --noEmit`).

Context: Don't Starve Together (family `dst`) was added to the sellable catalog TODAY and its landing page + blog post are already published live-on-staging, meaning a real customer could order it right now. A just-completed audit found a potential blocking bug: `lib/game-config.ts` has a `TOKEN` field (the Klei cluster authentication token, required for DST dedicated servers) that defaults to blank, with the config's own help text saying **"Required to run publicly."** It's unclear whether the DST dedicated server container will even successfully bind its UDP game port without this token — if it doesn't, the worker's own provisioning health check (`checkGamePortOpen` in `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()`) would time out and the customer's order would hard-fail right after they paid.

Your job:
1. **Determine ground truth first**: research (WebSearch, the DST dedicated server's own documentation, the specific Docker image used — check `prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts` for which image was chosen) exactly what happens when a DST dedicated server starts with NO cluster token set. Does it: (a) fail to bind the port / crash entirely, (b) bind the port and run but reject all client connections until a token is added, or (c) run in some kind of degraded/local-only mode? This determines the actual severity and the right fix.
2. **If it's blocking (a or effectively-unusable b)**: the real fix is almost certainly to make the token a required checkout-time input (like a "bring your own Klei account token" field, similar to how the game already needs the customer's own account for some other games in this catalog), rather than leaving it as a blank optional field discovered only in the settings tab after the fact. Research how a customer actually obtains a Klei cluster token (it's normally auto-generated by Klei's own official dedicated server tools when authenticated with a Klei account — confirm the exact real-world process) and determine if there's a way to make this smoother (e.g., clear checkout-time instructions + a guided settings-tab flow) even if full pre-fill isn't possible (a personal auth token generally can't be provided by Nxeon on the customer's behalf).
3. **Implement whichever fix is warranted**: at minimum, update the checkout flow / order confirmation / post-deploy instructions to clearly and immediately tell the customer this token is required and exactly how to get one and where to enter it (don't just leave it buried in an optional settings field with generic help text) — treat this with the same urgency as a checkout-blocking issue, since right now a paying customer could get a dead, unusable server with no clear signal why. If you determine the server is fully non-functional without it (can't bind port / can't be joined), consider whether the deploy wizard should require this field to be filled in AT CHECKOUT (before payment) rather than after, to avoid selling a broken experience — but only make this checkout-blocking change if you're confident that's the correct UX call; if unsure, prioritize very clear, prominent post-deploy guidance instead and flag the checkout-gating question for the owner.
4. Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, confirm clean.

This is time-sensitive since the product is already live — work efficiently but don't skip the ground-truth research step, a wrong guess here could make things worse. Report back (under 350 words): what you found about the token's actual necessity/severity, what you implemented, and whether you think checkout-time gating is warranted (with your reasoning) even if you didn't implement that specific change yourself.

/**
 * Inject `-e TYPE=<VARIANT>` into a Minecraft OsTemplate's setupScript from
 * `Server.gameVariant` (the customer's checkout choice — vanilla/paper/purpur/
 * fabric/forge, see lib/game-config.ts's MINECRAFT.variants).
 *
 * Found live 2026-08-30: this substitution never existed anywhere in the
 * provisioning pipeline. The OsTemplate's setupScript is one static string
 * with no `TYPE` at all, so `gameVariant` was captured at checkout, stored on
 * `Server`, and then completely ignored — every Minecraft customer got plain
 * Vanilla regardless of what they picked (or paid for a plugin-support tier
 * and had their manually-installed plugins never load, since Vanilla has no
 * plugin API at all). Diagnosed via a real customer ticket: the fix here is
 * minecraft-specific by design (it's the only family with a real variant
 * concept today) — generalize via `schemaFor(family)` if another family gains
 * one, rather than hardcoding a second family name here.
 *
 * Explicit and idempotent: always injects a `TYPE`, even for "vanilla" —
 * removes any reliance on the image's own default ever staying Vanilla — and
 * is a no-op if the script already names an explicit `TYPE` (never override
 * something a future per-family script sets on purpose).
 *
 * Kept in its own side-effect-free module (rather than inline in
 * worker/index.ts) so it can be unit tested directly — importing
 * worker/index.ts runs its top-level `main()` job-polling loop.
 */
export function applyGameVariant(setupScript: string, family: string | null, variant: string | null): string {
  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
  if (!variant) return setupScript;
  if (/-e\s+TYPE=/.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
  const type = variant.toUpperCase();
  return setupScript.replace(/(docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b)/, `$1 -e TYPE=${type}`);
}

62	 * escaping (`'\''`) so a customer-supplied string can never break out of the
63	 * quote and inject shell — the same safety property `validateConfig`'s own

65	 * (a `docker run` command line) since the injection surface differs from a
66	 * line-oriented remote config file.

72	): string {

74	  const schema = schemaFor(family);
75	  if (!schema) return setupScript;
76	  let out = setupScript;
77	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
78	    const raw = gameConfig[field.key];
79	    if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue;
80	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${field.key}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
81	    if (!re.test(out)) continue; // this field isn't docker-env-driven in this script — leave it alone

83	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${field.key}='${escaped}'`);
84	  }

input.title: Wire DST's Endless/Wilderness variant to GAME_MODE env var
input.tldr: Found while fixing the DST TOKEN checkout bug: customers who pick the Endless or Wilderness game mode at checkout always get a plain Survival server instead, because the setup script's GAME_MODE value is hardcoded and never wired to their choice.
input.prompt:
Context: on 2026-08-31 I fixed a blocking bug where Don't Starve Together (DST) dedicated servers couldn't start because the customer's checkout-time Klei cluster TOKEN was captured into Server.gameConfig but never substituted into the OsTemplate.setupScript's `docker run -e TOKEN='' ...` command (worker/index.ts's provision() never read Server.gameConfig at all — same root cause as the earlier Minecraft-TYPE bug fixed in worker/game-variant.ts's applyGameVariant). I added a general fix, `applyGameConfigEnv` in worker/game-variant.ts (wired into worker/index.ts's provision()), which substitutes any FamilySchema field whose key already exists in the setupScript as `-e KEY=...` with the customer's real gameConfig value.

While researching that, I found a SIBLING bug in the same family that this fix does NOT cover, because it's a variant issue, not a `ConfigField` issue: DST's FamilySchema (lib/game-config.ts, `DST` const) declares three variants — survival, endless, wilderness — matching DST's three real game modes. But prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts's DST setupScript hardcodes `-e GAME_MODE='survival'` as a static literal, and there is no equivalent of `applyGameVariant`'s Minecraft-TYPE substitution for DST's variant → GAME_MODE mapping. So a customer who picks "Endless" or "Wilderness" at checkout (Server.gameVariant gets set correctly) always gets a plain Survival server anyway — silently wrong, exactly like the pre-fix Minecraft TYPE bug that was already diagnosed and fixed for that family.

The fix is small and should follow the exact same pattern as applyGameVariant: in worker/game-variant.ts, either extend applyGameVariant to also handle `family === "dst"` (injecting/replacing `-e GAME_MODE=<VARIANT>` the same way TYPE is handled for minecraft — variant ids "survival"/"endless"/"wilderness" already match the env var's expected values verbatim, no uppercase transform needed unlike TYPE), or add a small parallel function. Wire it into worker/index.ts's provision() alongside the existing applyGameVariant call. Add unit tests in test/game-variant.test.ts mirroring the existing Minecraft TYPE tests (injects/replaces GAME_MODE, no-op for non-dst families, doesn't override an already-explicit GAME_MODE, idempotent).

Also worth a quick look while in this area: DST's `PASSWORD` ConfigField (lib/game-config.ts) has no corresponding `-e PASSWORD=` in prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts's DST setupScript at all — the yeetzone/dontstarvetogether image may not even support a server password via env var (worth checking its docs at github.com/yeet-zone/docker-dontstarvetogether). If it doesn't, the field's help text ("Blank = open server") is accidentally true today but for the wrong reason (nothing is wired, not "blank means open") and should either be removed from the schema or properly wired if the image does support a password via a different mechanism (e.g. cluster.ini). Low priority compared to the GAME_MODE fix above.

Work only in /opt/nxeon-staging (never /opt/nxeon prod). Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx tsx --test test/game-variant.test.ts`. Never run `npm run build` in the staging tree.

## Summary

**Ground truth on the token:** Confirmed severity (a) — an *online* DST cluster (the default when neither `OFFLINE_ENABLE` nor `LAN_ONLY` is set, which is exactly what the current `dst` setup script does) **refuses to start at all with no cluster token** — it's not a degraded/LAN-only fallback, it's a hard refusal. That means the container never binds UDP 10999, `checkGamePortOpen` in `worker/provision-health.ts` would time out, and `provision()` in `worker/index.ts` would hard-fail the job — the customer's order errors out right after paying, exactly as feared. Tokens are obtained free via the Klei account UI (`Play → Account → Generate Server Token`) or `accounts.klei.com/account/game/servers?game=DontStarveTogether` — this can't be pre-filled by Nxeon since it's personally auth-bound.

**Deeper bug found:** the checkout wizard's "Settings" step (where `DST.TOKEN` lives) already runs *before* payment — but I traced the pipeline and found `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()` never actually reads `Server.gameConfig` at all. Every family's checkout-time field values (not just DST's) were captured and stored but silently discarded — the VM always boots with the OS template's static default (`-e TOKEN=''`). So even requiring the field at checkout wouldn't have helped without also fixing this.

**Implemented (staging only):**
1. `lib/game-config.ts` — added `ConfigField.required`, marked `DST.TOKEN` required with clear step-by-step help text (URL + exact menu path), enforced in `validateConfig`'s string branch (blocks both checkout and settings-tab saves, server-side).
2. `worker/game-variant.ts` — new `applyGameConfigEnv()`, generalizing the existing Minecraft-TYPE precedent to substitute any customer `gameConfig` value into its matching `-e KEY=...` docker placeholder, with proper shell-quote escaping. Wired into `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()`.
3. `components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx` / `GameSettings.tsx` — required-field visual indicators (red "won't start without this" vs green checkmark) and a new checkout-blocking gate (`missingRequiredField`) that stops the customer reaching Review/Payment.
4. Tests added in `test/game-variant.test.ts` and `test/games.test.ts` (injection-safety, no-op cases, required rejection) — all pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.

**Checkout gating: yes, warranted and implemented** — ground truth confirmed the server is unambiguously non-functional without it, so blocking before payment is correct, not just cautious.

**Flagged as follow-up** (spawned, not fixed): DST's Endless/Wilderness variant is also silently ignored (`GAME_MODE` hardcoded to survival) — same root cause, separate fix.
